title: Temperature and pH Effects on Enzyme Activity
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: High School Biology
description: Students predict how temperature, pH, and thermostability reshape enzyme activity curves while connecting those shifts to molecular explanations.

educational.topic: Enzyme kinetics, temperature, and pH effects
learningObjectives: Predict how adjusting optimal temperature or pH shifts an enzyme's relative activity curve.
Explain why excessive heat denatures the active site while pH extremes mis-ionize catalytic residues.
Compare human enzymes, pepsin, and Taq polymerase by interpreting preset curves and curve width.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of enzyme structure and substrate binding
Familiarity with kinetic energy, hydrogen bonding, and ionization
Ability to read trends on Cartesian graphs

keyQuestions: What molecular events explain the decline in activity at the cursor's position?
How do the optimal conditions of each preset align with its native environment?
commonMisconceptions: Learners may assume that higher temperatures always speed catalysis.
Students may think pH changes only scale activity instead of altering residue charge.
assessmentOpportunities: Collect written predictions before and after loading each preset curve.
Use exit tickets asking students to justify the activity drop using collisions, denaturation, or protonation.
